Lemma
[$\tilde{U}$ solves the one-dimensional wave equation] ↗ lem:euler-poisson-darboux-equation ↗ lem:wave-equation-useful-identities 1. ch2:2.4-lem-3\group Wave Equation

The transformed average satisfies \[ \widetilde U_{tt}-\widetilde U_{rr}=0, \qquad \widetilde U(r,0)=\widetilde G(r), \qquad \widetilde U_t(r,0)=\widetilde H(r), \qquad \widetilde U(0,t)=0. \]
Proof

\sketch The identities in subsubsection lem:wave-equation-useful-identities and $n=2k+1$ give

\[ \widetilde U_{rr} =\left(\frac1r\partial _r\right)^{k-1} \left[r^{2k-1}\left(U_{rr}+\frac{n-1}{r}U_r\right)\right] =\widetilde U_{tt}. \]

The expansion in powers of $r$ gives the boundary value at $r=0$.

□

With $\gamma _n=1\cdot 3\cdot 5\cdots (n-2)$, d'Alembert's formula yields \[ (31)\qquad u(x,t)=\frac1{\gamma _n}\left[ \partial _t\left(\frac1t\partial _t\right)^{(n-3)/2} \left(t^{n-2}\fint _{\partial B(x,t)}g\, dS\right) +\left(\frac1t\partial _t\right)^{(n-3)/2} \left(t^{n-2}\fint _{\partial B(x,t)}h\, dS\right) \right]. \]
